newsitem.title: USA: First of Michigan gains from cost controls.
newsitem.headline: First of Michigan gains from cost controls.

text.p: First of Michigan Capital Corp said on Friday that its fiscal 1996 fourth quarter and year- end earnings benefited from expense controls and a major effort to be the dominant broker-dealer in the Michigan.
Earlier, First of Michigan reported earnings for its fiscal 1996 fourth quarter ended September 27, 1996 rose to $725,414, or $0.27 a share, up from $9,490, or $0.01, in the year ago period.
Revenues fell to $16.9 million from $18.5 million.

Earnings for its fiscal year rose to $1.8 million, or $0.66, including a charge of about $600,000, or $0.22, from one-time costs of a realignment of the company's operations and management structure taken in the second quarter.
Lower fiscal fourth revenues reflected reduced revenues from fees and syndicate activities due to market volatility during the period, president Kenneth Eich said in a statement.

Higher fiscal 1996 revenues reflected increased retail commissions generated from listed and over-the-counter stock business, increased revenues from mutual fund transactions and slightly higher interest revenues.
First of Michigan provides investment services to retail and institutional customers through 32 offices in Michigan.
